issues.display_title: Issue #467: Preview: level switch blocks main thread up to ~3.4s — buildGrid runs on every switch
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Switching levels on /preview/[projectId] (and /v/[key]) freezes the page — on a large project (af88d2e4, airport) switching Level 1 → Level 2 blocks the main thread for ~3.4 s (measured via longtask + CPU profile). The editor switches instantly.

Root cause

PreviewOverlay.tsx recomputes the routing wallGrid (buildGrid) in a useMemo on every level switch. The comment claims "cheap: ~1ms", but for a large building the grid rasterizes the whole bbox at 4 px cells with a point-in-polygon test per cell per area — profiled at ~2.6 s (pointInPolygon 1284 ms + buildGrid 1182 ms + clearanceField 105 ms).

The grid's only consumer is the dev-mode debug nav-grid overlay in useDirectionMapLayers (gated by devMode && debugGrid). Real routing (planMultiLevelRoute) builds its own grids and never reads it.

Fix

Gate the memo so the grid is only built when the debug overlay can actually render it:

if (!devMode || !debugGrid || !singleLevel) return null;

Acceptance criteria

  • Level switch in preview no longer runs buildGrid when the debug grid overlay is off
  • Dev-mode "Grid" toggle still renders the nav-grid overlay
  • Measured long task on level switch drops from ~3.4 s to sub-second on the airport project

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Gated the wallGrid memo in PreviewOverlay.tsx behind devMode && debugGrid — the routing nav-grid is now only built when the dev-mode debug overlay can actually render it. Real routing (planMultiLevelRoute) was never a consumer; public preview/live level switches no longer pay the buildGrid cost.

Measured on the reported project (af88d2e4, airport):

  • Before: switching Level 1 → Level 2 = single 3413 ms long task (CPU profile: pointInPolygon 1284 ms + buildGrid 1182 ms + clearanceField 105 ms)
  • After: worst long task 178 ms, total blocked ~0.7–1.0 s spread across small tasks (normal GeoJSON rebuild for a building this size)
  • Dev-mode "Grid" toggle still builds and renders the nav-grid overlay on demand

Files changed: src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx (memo gate + corrected the stale "cheap: ~1ms" comment)

Verified: vitest 585 passed, eslint clean, tsc --noEmit clean, before/after browser profiling via Playwright.

issues.display_title: Issue #468: Map markers: per-frame display churn forces full reflow every frame on dense projects
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The editor Map view (and preview/live, same component) stutters on marker-dense projects — reported on project 43fada28 (262 objects, heavy pano-chip overlap): visible lag while panning/rotating the map.

Root cause

MapObjectMarkers's per-frame reposition() uses style.display to cull off-screen markers (pass 1) and hide decluttered markers (pass 3), then reads offsetWidth/offsetHeight of every on-screen marker (pass 2). With overlapping markers the declutter pass flips display: none ↔ "" on the same buttons every frame, so layout is invalidated every frame and pass 2 forces a full reflow every frame.

Measured in-situ on the reported project (128 markers in DOM): size reads cost 0.4 ms with clean layout vs 9.2 ms with the display churn — more than half the 16 ms frame budget burned on reflow before MapLibre/three.js even render. CPU profile during a drag: reposition ≈ 5.3 s self-time.

Fix

  • Switch the initial style and all three reposition() write sites from display to visibility.
  • Write only when the value actually changes.

visibility does not affect layout, so layout stays clean and the per-frame size reads become free. visibility: hidden elements are still unclickable and invisible (same behavior) and remain measurable (display: none reports 0×0), which is also more correct for declutter.

Acceptance criteria

  • No forced reflow per frame from reposition() (size-read cost back to ~0.4 ms)
  • Culled/decluttered markers still hidden and non-interactive
  • Marker drag, hover bubbles, dot mode, declutter behavior unchanged

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Switched marker hide/show in MapObjectMarkers from style.display to style.visibility (initial JSX style + all three reposition() write sites), with a change-guard so unchanged frames write nothing. Layout is never dirtied by the per-frame loop, so pass 2's offsetWidth/offsetHeight reads no longer force a reflow. Hidden markers stay non-interactive and invisible, and remain measurable (more correct for declutter than display:none's 0×0).

Measured on the reported project (43fada28, 262 objects / 128 markers in DOM):

  • In-situ size-read benchmark: 9.2 ms per frame with display churn → 0.4 ms clean
  • CPU profile of an identical drag: reposition.sized self-time ~4.8 s → ~0.1 s (dense area), 0 ms over empty area
  • Declutter still hides overlapping markers (88/128 visible on load), drag/hover/dot-mode unchanged

Applies to editor Map view, /preview, /v/[key], /embed — same component.

Files changed: src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx

Verified: vitest 585 passed, eslint clean, tsc --noEmit clean, before/after browser profiling via Playwright.

Commit: 903d24d

issues.display_title: Issue #470: Edit Levels: drag-reorder must also reorder canvasData.levels (root of #469)
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Dragging floors in the editor's Edit Levels modal reorders only floorConfigs (EditLevelModal.tsx handleDragOver). canvasData.levels — the order the 3D stack, FloorSelector, preview/live floor list, and levelsAtOrBelow all trust — is never touched. One drag permanently diverges the two orders, and persistence saves/restores them independently, so the mismatch survives into /preview and /v/[key] (#469).

Side effects once diverged: the editor panel level dropdown and FloorSelector list floors in different orders; auto-naming renumbers names by floorConfigs index while the physical stack keeps the old order; undo/redo can silently revert a config-only reorder (no history snapshot on setFloorConfigs).

Fix

In handleDragOver, reorder canvasData.levels to the same id order as the new floorConfigs (via setCanvasData, which also pushes a history snapshot — fixing the undo hole for reorders). Drag becomes the authoritative floor-order tool and doubles as a repair tool for already-diverged projects.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dragging in Edit Levels reorders both floorConfigs and canvasData.levels identically
  • 3D stack / FloorSelector / preview reflect the new order immediately
  • Undo restores the pre-drag order

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

handleDragEnd in EditLevelModal.tsx now commits the modal's new floor order to canvasData.levels via a new pure helper levelsInConfigOrder(levels, configs) in src/lib/editor/levels.ts (orphan levels — no config yet — keep their tail position; dangling config ids are skipped). Committed once per drop, not per dragOver, so one setCanvasData = one history snapshot — which also makes the reorder undoable (previously a config-only reorder had no history entry and undo silently reverted it).

The 3D stack, FloorSelector, preview/live floor list and levelsAtOrBelow all follow the drag immediately, and dragging doubles as a repair tool for already-diverged projects (#469).

Files changed:

  • src/components/editor/EditLevelModal.tsx — commit order on drag end
  • src/lib/editor/levels.ts — levelsInConfigOrder helper
  • src/lib/editor/__tests__/levels.test.ts — +2 tests (reorder, orphan/dangling handling)

Verified: vitest 587 passed, eslint clean, tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #471: Wizard: retried floor scan appends its level out of order in rebuildTwin
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

StepGenerate.rebuildTwin builds canvasData.levels from resultsRef Map insertion order. The first generation pass is sequential so order matches floorConfigs — but a floor that FAILED on the first pass is absent from the map, and when retried (Retry Failed / row Retry) its first set() appends it at the END. Result: canvasData.levels = completion order (e.g. [1,3,4,2]) while floorConfigs stays [1,2,3,4]. This is the likely original corruption behind #469 — the mismatch persists into every viewer.

Fix

Order the merge by floorConfigs, not map insertion:

const entries = floorConfigs
  .map((c) => [c.id, resultsRef.current.get(c.id)] as const)
  .filter((e): e is [string, ScanResult] => !!e[1]);

Acceptance criteria

  • A floor that fails then succeeds on retry lands at its floorConfigs position in canvasData.levels
  • Twin levels order matches too (same entries feed mergeResults)

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

rebuildTwin in StepGenerate.tsx now assembles its entries by iterating floorConfigs and looking results up in the map, instead of spreading the results Map's insertion order. A floor that fails the first pass and succeeds on Retry now lands at its floorConfigs position in both canvasData.levels and the Digital Twin's levels (same entries feed mergeResults), instead of being appended after later floors — the likely original corruption behind #469.

Files changed: src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx

Verified: vitest 585 passed, eslint clean, tsc --noEmit clean. (Ordering is a 3-line declarative map/filter; covered by typecheck + existing step-generate machine tests, no dedicated test added.)

issues.display_title: Issue #472: Add Panorama: imported panorama resolves its floor by positional index into canvasData.levels
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

placeMarkers.ts resolves an imported panorama's target floor with canvasData.levels[p.level] — a positional index. Any divergence or reorder of the levels array (e.g. #469-style corruption, Edit Levels drag) silently retargets panoramas onto the wrong floor at import time.

Fix

Resolve the target level through a stable mapping instead of a raw index into the live store array (e.g. snapshot the level-id list once at import start, or map p.level through floorConfigs order — pick whichever matches the import payload's floor-numbering semantics after reading the flow).

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing panoramas after a floor reorder places them on the intended floors
  • Existing single-floor / ordered-project imports unchanged

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

groupPanosByLevel now resolves a pano's tour level index through floorConfigs order (the user-visible floor order) instead of indexing canvasData.levels positionally. On a diverged project (#469) tour floor N lands on the floor the user sees at position N, not whatever happens to sit at that index in the levels array. With no floorConfigs passed the raw levels index remains the fallback (the arrays only diverge via floorConfigs edits, so without configs they cannot have diverged). Both callers (Add Panorama import, Apply Location modal) pass the store's floorConfigs.

Files changed:

  • src/components/editor/add-panorama/placeMarkers.ts — index via floorConfigs
  • src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/AddPanoramaButton.tsx, src/components/editor/add-panorama/ApplyLocationModal.tsx — pass floorConfigs

issues.display_title: Issue #485: Information: per-day weekly hours with Closed/Open/Open 24h (PRD #473 T5)

Scope

  • Monday–Sunday each configurable as Closed / Open / Open 24h

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Returns null for no hours. This is the single reader every consumer (editor prefill now, visitor card in T9) goes through.

issues.display_title: Issue #494: Visitor hours: building-local open/closed status via offline timezone lookup (PRD #473 12.8)
issues.main_description_html:
Part of PRD #473 — Phase 3 follow-up. Decision 12.8: open/closed status should use the building's local time when available, visitor device time as fallback.

Approach (no backend)

  • tz-lookup (small, offline) resolves the project's pinned location (lat/lng, already in the model) to an IANA timezone.
  • The browser's built-in tz database (Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone) computes the building-local weekday/date/time — no server involvement.
  • openStatus / effectiveDayHours accept a clock abstraction; the visitor card feeds them the building clock, falling back to device time when the project has no location.

Acceptance criteria

  • Project with a pinned location: open/closed status follows the building's timezone, not the visitor's
  • No location → device time (current behavior)
  • Special-hours date matching uses the building-local date
  • No API/backend changes

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Fully frontend — no API change:

  • tz-lookup (new dep, offline lat/lng → IANA timezone) + a local type declaration (src/types/tz-lookup.d.ts; the package ships none).
  • src/lib/hours.ts: new ClockParts abstraction — deviceClock(now), zonedClock(timeZone, now) (reads the wall clock of any IANA zone through Intl.DateTimeFormat's built-in tz database), and buildingClock(location, now) (pin → timezone → zoned clock; null/out-of-range → device clock). effectiveDayHours / openStatus accept Date | ClockParts, so all existing callers/tests keep working; special-hours date matching now happens in the building-local date.
  • Visitor card: PreviewOverlay passes the project pin into PreviewInfoCard → HoursSection computes status/today from buildingClock(location). No pin = device time (12.8 fallback, unchanged behavior).

Tests: +3 — zonedClock against Asia/Jakarta (UTC+7, incl. date rollover), buildingClock pin resolution + null fallback, and an open/closed divergence case where the building is already on the next day. Suite 606 passed, eslint clean, tsc clean.
